messages:
sam: Heads-up — I’m seeing a ~3x jump in 'estimated_units' on the Embeddings route for tenant `foo-inc` after the prebatcher change. timeline matches mixed-dim requests starting at 14:02. anyone tracking?

lina: saw that alert too. spikes are in the per-route units graph, not raw token counts. looks like mixed dims caused our estimator to pick the worst-case dim for whole batch. :thinking:

mo: yikes. that matches the prebatcher heuristic we added — it picks the max dim across batch to compute unit cost. we assumed it’d be rare.

ben: quick question — are we sure this affects billing metrics or just console visuals?

sam: both. backend counter 'embed_units_v1' jumped and our billing preview picked it up. QA also flagged customer support about surprising cost.

qa-ale: got a support thread. customer sent payloads with [128, 1024, 128] dims in same request. they expected proportional cost, not max-dim billing.

mo: root cause: router coalesces mixed-dim items into one prebatch to optimize throughput then estimator scales by max_dim. naive but cheaper in latency. need to decide policy: preserve throughput vs fair billing.

lina: Proposal: add a per-request header 'X-Embed-Dim-Hint' that clients can optionally set to declare dims so estimator can compute accurate per-item units instead of max. fallback remains current behavior.

sam: +1 for opt-in header. We should also expose a console toggle to enable per-tenant accurate accounting (costly compute).

ben: from runtime POV we can compute sum(units_i) cheaply if header present. Otherwise existing fast path stays. we should add telemetry flags: sample and count how often mixed-dim happens and extra compute cost.

mo: suggested rollout: 1) add header support in router/runtime + feature flag 2) sample 1% traffic with header-enabled to gather delta 3) console chart for 'estimated_units_adjusted' 4) if delta < 5% adopt opt-in default for new tenants

sre-ryan: watch out for perf regression on high-concurrency tenants. sampling must be small. also add circuit to fallback if per-request compute pushes latency > SLO.

lina: UX for console: show per-tenant toggle 'Prefer proportional embed units' with note about slightly higher CPU. add a tooltip and link to docs. console-bot can create a docs stub.

console-bot: created docs stub: /docs/embeddings/dim-hint-accounting (draft).

sam: for API docs snippet, proposed curl: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Embed-Dim-Hint: 256,1024,256" \
  -d '{"inputs": [[...],[...],[...]]}'
```

mo: small nit — header list parse might be brittle. maybe allow `X-Embed-Unit-Estimate: 3,12,3` (units per item) instead so clients don't need to know units formula.

ben: agree. unit-estimate is friendlier. runtime still validates length matches items.

sam: telemetry plan: emit counters \`embed_units_reported_v2\` (by tenant, sampled) and a trace tag when header used. console team can hook these into a delta chart.

lina: I'll wire a dashboard mock: breakdown columns: raw_tokens, old_estimated_units, adjusted_estimated_units, delta_pct. quick toggle to view sampled vs all.

qa-ale: also add a support playbook snippet explaining why earlier customers might see lower apparent cost and how to opt in.

mo: implementation tasks: router PR to accept header and compute adjusted units (fast path off), runtime flag, metric emission, unit tests; console PR for toggle + chart; docs + support playbook.

ben: can we ship header parsing + metric without UI first? that lets us sample immediately.

sam: yes, do backend-first. we'll gate sampling via feature-flag. devs: please add a Canary label so we can flip for 10 tenants initially.

sre-ryan: I'll add a rate-limit/circuit to prevent any one tenant from causing CPU spikes. alert if sampled-latency > 20% SLO.

deploy-bot: Canary feature-flag 'embed_dim_estimator_v2' created. owners: @mo, @lina. :eyes:

sam: thanks. assign tickets and let's sync tomorrow standup if anyone hits blockers. :thumbsup:
